title: New parts after the change keep the work order's tier
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin whose role has 'Settings — Parts', 'See Financial Data', 'Customers — View', 'Customers — Create & Edit', 'Work Orders — Order Parts' and 'Work Order Lines — Create & Edit'.
  • Have a new tier for this test, tier A, with a name no other tier uses.
  • Have a new matrix for this test, matrix A, pricing a new category made for this test, category A, with one range from $0.00: Default Markup % 50, tier A Markup % 20.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, on tier A for work orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer B, on Default for work orders.
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 1, for customer A, with one labor line (line 1).
  • Use a desktop browser window at least 1440 pixels wide, at 100% zoom, so every column of the page shows.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Open work order 1's three-dot menu.
  3. Click Change Customer.
  4. Pick customer B.
  5. Click Update Customer.
  6. Click Add Part under line 1.
  7. Type a description in Description (for example Test part).
  8. Type 1 in Qty.
  9. Pick category A in Category.
  10. Type 20.00 in Cost.
  11. Click Save.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The menu lists Change Customer, Split Work Order and Back to Work Orders.

Step 3:

  • The Change Customer dialog opens.

Step 4:

  • The amber note shows.

Step 5:

  • Work order 1 now shows customer B.

Step 6:

  • A new part row opens under line 1 with Part number, Description, Qty, Category, Cost and Sell price boxes and Save and Cancel.

Step 7:

  • Description holds the typed text.

Step 8:

  • Qty holds 1.

Step 9:

  • Category shows category A.

Step 10:

  • Cost holds 20.00 as typed.

Step 11:

  • The new part sells at $24.00 ($20.00 × 1.20 = $24.00, tier A).
  • It is not priced at Default's $30.00 ($20.00 × 1.50).
